title: Body Language Codes (Unit 5)

points: Walk with drooping shoulders indicates discouragement; erect walk indicates enthusiasm
Forward leaning indicates excitement or eagerness; turning back indicates neglecting or avoiding someone
Standing ovation indicates appreciation; hands in pocket indicates immature behavior
Cross legs or arms while sitting or standing indicate disagreement with the sender
Tips: do not droop shoulders, look straight while walking, lift feet clearly, avoid slouching and crossing limbs
Gesture means a motion of hand, head or limbs used to reinforce something that is said
Waving indicates hello or good bye; making a fist indicates anger; thumbs up shows appreciation or agreement
Scratching head indicates thinking; nodding head indicates acceptance; shrugging shoulders indicates indifference
Locking hands behind the back indicates arrogance; upraised hand indicates request for patience
Tips: avoid aggressive gestures, avoid hands in pockets, keep hand gestures above the waist
Face is considered "an index of mind"; facial expressions are involuntary so they convey real emotions
A smile expresses friendliness and affection; raised eyebrows convey surprise; a frown shows dislike or suspicion
Furrowed forehead and lines on forehead indicate worries; pursing lips indicates lack of confidence; smirk indicates arrogance
Yawning indicates tiredness or boredom
Eye contact establishes rapport; avoiding it indicates fear, doubt and nervousness; winking indicates lying or hiding
Dress and appearance show status and attitude; adapt appearance to the occasion (formal, semi-formal, informal)
Vocalic is the study of the quality of the voice, also called paralanguage
Voice tones convey meaning: commanding (officer), shaky (nervous), high pitched (fear), gentle (respect), resonant (dynamic)
Silence is studied under vocalic; silence speaks louder than words and can be considered effective feedback
Haptics is derived from Greek meaning "to touch or grasp"; it conveys emotions like affection, anger and encouragement
Negative haptics convey anger, displeasure, hate and violence (slap, prick, handshake with pressure)
A handshake with pressure indicates domination
Positive haptics convey love, affection, respect and encouragement (pat on back, handshake, touching feet, touching shoulder)

quiz.q: Which posture indicates excitement or eagerness?
quiz.why: Forward leaning indicates excitement or eagerness.
Thumbs up shows appreciation or agreement.
The face is considered "an index of mind"; it exhibits attitudes.

quiz.q: Which eye behaviour indicates lying or hiding?
quiz.why: Winking eyes indicate lying or hiding.

quiz.q: The study of the quality of voice is called:
quiz.why: The study of the quality of the voice is called vocalic (also called paralanguage).
A handshake with pressure is a negative haptic that indicates domination.

quiz.q: Touching the feet of a person is a gesture of:
quiz.why: To touch feet is to show respect — a positive haptic.

options: Speaks louder than words and can be effective feedback
quiz.why: Silence speaks louder than words and can be considered effective feedback; it is studied under vocalic.
